why_this_device: Campbell (2002) organised the elastic limit with pressure-controlled shear; R1-R4 used a constant-volume cell and could never dilate. This device is the repository's constant-stress servo shear box.

observables.kappa: k_n/(rho d^3 gdot^2), gdot = measured bulk shear rate
observables.tau_star: tau/(rho d^2 gdot^2), tau = measured bulk shear stress
observables.inertial_number: gdot d/sqrt(P/rho), P = measured bulk pressure

predictions.P2_exponent: |beta_CP - beta_CV| <= 0.15 -> kappa is the sole control
predictions.P4_concentration: phi monotone in kappa (higher kappa -> denser)
predictions.P6_collapse: kn rungs at fixed I land on the rate-ladder curve (diagnostic)

known_degeneracy: on this path kappa and I are not independent: kappa I^2 = k_n/(d P), so tau* = mu kappa dP/k_n and beta = 1 + d ln mu/d ln kappa + d ln P/d ln kappa. The constant-pressure exponent is therefore NOT an independent measurement of the anchor's beta; P2 is reported as a consistency check with the structural prediction, not as confirmation.

known_untestable.campbell_numeric_table: full text closed (paywall) - coefficient leg WITHHELD
known_untestable.dimension: this device is 3-D, R1-R4 are 2-D; coefficients are not transferable across dimension and are compared only as declared deviation
known_untestable.overlap: the servo device does not return particle overlaps; the small-overlap gate is an analytic proxy 1/(3 kappa I^2), declared as a proxy, not a measurement

constant_pressure_smooth.note: read when present; the smooth-wall round is the diagnosis that motivates this variant
